faq.q: What's the difference between AI Precise and Fast mode?
faq.a: AI Precise downloads a roughly 40MB model (@imgly/background-removal) on first use, then cuts out the subject on any background — typically 20–60 seconds on a laptop, running on your device. Fast mode is instant but only works on solid backgrounds: it flood-fills from the four corner pixels using a detection threshold you set (5–120) and a Sobel edge check. If the AI model fails to load, it falls back to Fast mode.

faq.q: Which output sizes and formats are built in for ID photos?
faq.a: Besides keeping the original size, the Output Size dropdown offers 200×230 (SSC/UPSC), 300×350 (ID card), 413×531 (passport 35×45mm), 600×800 (large passport) and 150×200 (thumbnail). The subject is scaled to fit while preserving aspect ratio and centred. Output format is PNG, JPEG or WEBP; the quality slider only appears for JPEG and WEBP since PNG is lossless.

faq.q: Can I use a gradient or transparent background?
faq.a: Yes. Tick Gradient Background and pick two colours for a linear gradient, or choose the transparent (checkerboard) preset, white, blue, red, grey, dark blue, green, black, or any custom colour. Note: if you pick transparent but export as JPEG, which has no alpha channel, the tool fills white instead of leaving the area black.

faq.q: Can I process several photos at once?
faq.a: Yes. Drop multiple files and it processes them in a queue showing per-file progress, with individual download buttons and a Download All as ZIP option (via JSZip) when more than one succeeds. A Max Width setting (up to 2000px, or no limit) can cap exported width to shrink large photos; it only ever reduces, never upscales.
